data.title: First-Party Dispute Anomaly — Chargeback with Delivery Confirmation, Device Match, and No Merchant Contact
data.description: Detects high-confidence friendly fraud by identifying chargebacks where three independent indicators contradict the dispute claim: (1) delivery was confirmed for the original order, (2) the device fingerprint filing the dispute matches the device used for the original purchase, and (3) no merchant contact was attempted before the chargeback was filed. The triple correlation of delivery evidence, device match, and merchant bypass is a strong signal that the cardholder is the original purchaser who received the goods and chose to file a chargeback rather than a legitimate return. 84% of consumers find chargebacks simpler than contacting merchants, creating systemic abuse of the dispute mechanism.

detection.condition: selection AND filter_delivery AND filter_device_match AND filter_no_merchant_contact

enrichment_required.source: Shipping carrier delivery confirmation (signed, GPS-verified, photo proof)
Comparison of device fingerprint at dispute filing vs. original purchase
Merchant CRM/support records — any contact from cardholder between transaction and dispute

queries.cql:
// CQL for First-Party Dispute Anomaly Detection — DL-0191
// Triple-correlated friendly fraud: delivery + device match + no merchant contact
Chargebacks
| dispute_type = "chargeback"
| dispute_date >= now() - 30d
| delivery_confirmed = true
| device_fingerprint_match = true
| merchant_contact_prior = false OR merchant_contact_prior = null
| days_delivery_to_dispute := round((dispute_date - delivery_date) / 86400, 0)
| sort(dispute_amount, order=desc)
queries.sql:
-- SQL: First-Party Dispute Anomaly Detection
-- Chargeback with delivery confirmation, device match, no merchant contact
SELECT
  d.dispute_id,
  d.cardholder_id,
  d.merchant_id,
  d.dispute_amount,
  d.dispute_reason_code,
  d.dispute_date,
  t.transaction_date,
  t.delivery_confirmed,
  t.delivery_date,
  DATEDIFF(DAY, t.delivery_date, d.dispute_date) AS days_delivery_to_dispute,
  t.device_fingerprint AS purchase_device,
  d.device_fingerprint AS dispute_device,
  CASE WHEN t.device_fingerprint = d.device_fingerprint THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
    AS device_match,
  mc.last_contact_date AS merchant_contact_date
FROM chargebacks d
JOIN transactions t ON d.original_transaction_id = t.transaction_id
LEFT JOIN merchant_contacts mc ON d.cardholder_id = mc.customer_id
  AND d.merchant_id = mc.merchant_id
  AND mc.contact_date BETWEEN t.transaction_date AND d.dispute_date
WHERE d.dispute_date >= DATEADD(DAY, -30, CURRENT_DATE)
  AND t.delivery_confirmed = 1
  AND t.device_fingerprint = d.device_fingerprint
  AND mc.contact_id IS NULL
ORDER BY d.dispute_amount DESC
queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL: First-Party Dispute Anomaly Detection")`
`comment("Triple-correlated friendly fraud: delivery + device match + no merchant contact")`
index=flame_payments sourcetype=flame:dispute_management
  dispute_type="chargeback"
| lookup delivery_lookup original_transaction_id
    OUTPUT delivery_confirmed, delivery_date
| lookup device_lookup original_transaction_id
    OUTPUT purchase_device_fingerprint
| lookup merchant_contact_lookup cardholder_id, merchant_id
    OUTPUT merchant_contact_prior
| where delivery_confirmed="true"
  AND dispute_device_fingerprint=purchase_device_fingerprint
  AND (merchant_contact_prior="false" OR isnull(merchant_contact_prior))
| eval days_delivery_to_dispute = round(
    (strptime(dispute_date, "%Y-%m-%d") - strptime(delivery_date, "%Y-%m-%d")) / 86400, 0)
| table dispute_id, cardholder_id, merchant_id, dispute_amount,
        dispute_reason_code, dispute_date, delivery_date,
        days_delivery_to_dispute, purchase_device_fingerprint
| sort - dispute_amount

references: Chargeflow, Friendly Fraud Statistics 2025 — 84% simplicity preference
falsepositives: Legitimate disputes where the product was defective but cardholder did not contact merchant
Shared devices where a different household member made the purchase
Delivery marked as confirmed but actually misdelivered (e.g., left at wrong address)
